subject: VM evidence & operational notes — compact exec summary and pen-test addendum
messages:
From: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@novatrust.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: concise VM evidence + pen-test summary for procurement review

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick call this morning. Procurement wants a short, consumable package that we can circulate to the internal risk committee: an executive summary of your vulnerability management posture, a short pen-test addendum (high-level findings + remediation status), SBOM inventory for hosted components, and your patch SLA commitments for critical/important issues.

Two asks:
- Can you provide a one-page exec summary we can give to non-technical stakeholders?
- We’ll need a machine-readable SBOM inventory (CSV ok) and a short note on how you score/normalize risk across SAST/DAST findings so we can map to our internal risk taxonomy.

Target timeline: procurement review on Friday (09/17). Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Michael Sanders
Senior Procurement Manager
Novatrust Financial

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: concise VM evidence + pen-test summary for procurement review

Marissa/Ben — forwarding Michael’s request. Procurement needs a compact deliverable set by Friday 9/17 for Novatrust (HT-2027-NT-0893). Key pieces: 1-page executive summary, pen-test addendum with remediation status, SBOM CSV, and a short explanation of how we normalize SAST/DAST severity to a single risk score.

I’ve attached the template we typically use for exec summaries and the standard SBOM extract script output sample. Can you take lead? Marissa on pen-test addendum + remediation status; Ben on SBOM CSV and risk-normalization blurb. I’ll review and then send to Michael.

Constraints: keep the executive summary one page; no raw log attachments in the external packet. Use Drive link for large artefacts.

Thx — V

[Attachment: exec-summary-template.docx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: concise VM evidence + pen-test summary for procurement review

Vanessa / Ben — quick status update:

1) Executive summary: Drafted a single-page PDF that covers our VM lifecycle (scan cadence, triage SLA, patch SLA, responsible teams) and a short metrics snapshot (avg time-to-fix criticals, recent pen-test remediation rate). Will attach PDF named "redwood_vm_exec_summary.pdf" when finalized.

2) Pen-test addendum: I pulled the August 2027 external engagement summary. High-level: 3 medium findings (dependency hardening), 1 low (info disclosure), 0 criticals. All medium findings are scheduled for remediation; two already mitigated in the 2027.08.18 release. I’ll create a bullet list with status (Open / In progress / Closed), remediation owner, and expected close dates.

3) SBOM: Ben — please confirm you can export the hosted-service SBOM slice as CSV scoped to runtime deps only (no developer-only packages). Compliance asked specifically for runtime-only inventory.

4) Risk normalization: I propose a short paragraph explaining that we map SAST/DAST categories into a single risk score via: CVSS base score (where available), exploitability heuristics, exposure (internet-facing vs internal), and compensating controls (WAF, runtime hardening). We then bucket to Novatrust taxonomy via a mapping table (we can include as appendix).

I’ve attached the pen-test artifact bundle (pen-test-addendum-2027-08.tar.gz) and a CSV sample for the SBOM layout.

Marissa
Sr. Security PM — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pen-test-addendum-2027-08.tar.gz]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@novatrust.com>, Compliance Team <compliance@novatrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: concise VM evidence + pen-test summary for procurement review

Michael — attaching the compact package for Novatrust procurement review. Contents: 1-page executive summary (redwood_vm_exec_summary.pdf), pen-test addendum (high-level summary + remediation table), SBOM runtime inventory (sbom-inventory-2027-07.csv), and a short note on our risk-normalization approach (in the exec summary appendix).

Summary highlights (one-line bullets for your risk committee):
- No open criticals from external pen-test (Aug 2027); three medium items: two remediated, one scheduled for 2027-09-22 release.
- Patch SLAs: criticals 48 hours target, important 7 days target for production-hosted services; measured median for last 12 months: criticals 22 hours, important 4.1 days.
- SBOM: runtime-only CSV attached; includes package name, version, checksum, source, and license.
- Risk normalization: we map SAST/DAST to CVSS where possible and layer runtime exposure + exploitability signals to derive a normalized 0-100 risk score for prioritization; mapping table included in appendix.

Attachments: redwood_vm_exec_summary.pdf (pdf), pen-test-addendum-2027-08.tar.gz (archive, Drive link below), sbom-inventory-2027-07.csv (csv).

Drive link for larger artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDummyDriveLink

Please let us know if you want any redlines or a one-page slide for the board. We can also provide anonymized sample CVE mapping CSV if procurement needs a machine-parseable mapping.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood_vm_exec_summary.pdf; sbom-inventory-2027-07.csv]

From: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@novatrust.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@novatrust.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Request: concise VM evidence + pen-test summary for procurement review

Vanessa — thanks, that’s very helpful and nicely condensed. A couple of clarifications for the committee before Friday: 
1) For the pen-test addendum, can you confirm which findings were "remediated" vs "mitigated" (we need to know if the code change shipping closed the issue or if an operational control blocks the exploit path)?
2) For the SBOM CSV, could you add a column for "runtime_scope" (e.g., "api-gateway", "ingest-worker") so we can map packages to our asset inventory?
3) For the risk normalization: can you provide the mapping table (even a small sample) that maps CVSS buckets to your 0-100 score?

If you can reply with those three small edits by 12:00pm PT today, we can move the packet to the review queue.

Best,
Michael

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Request: concise VM evidence + pen-test summary for procurement review

Marissa / Ben — Michael asked three quick follow-ups (see below). Can we get the changes live in the packet and resend by 12:00pm PT? I’ve captured the asks:

- Pen-test: mark each finding as Remediated (code change shipped) vs Mitigated (operational control) and include the PR/issue link where available (redact internal ticket details if needed; a sanitized link is fine).
- SBOM CSV: add a runtime_scope column (examples: api-gateway, worker-ingest, realtime-inference). Ben — please scope to runtime-only and include runtime_scope.
- Risk mapping sample: provide a 3-row sample mapping CVSS ranges to our normalized score (0-100) and a one-sentence explanation of compensating control adjustments.

Marissa — can you update the pen-test status table and resave the addendum as pen-test-addendum-2027-08.v2.tar.gz (archive of summary + sanitized PR links)? Ben — update the SBOM CSV and add a sample mapping file (risk-mapping-sample.csv). I’ll repackage and send to Michael ASAP.

Thanks — V

[This message contains no attachments]
